page_states: The remaining case is stated as mathring T intersect Gamma nonempty. A hull C is defined from mathring T union the base interval, intersected with Gamma; large inserted closed brackets surround the originally open base interval.
The page claims C is contained in T minus the two sides through s, and that vertices of partial C lying in mathring T are vertices of Gamma.
It asserts an interior vertex exists and invokes lemma IV to obtain y outside the vertex set of partial C, with y in C, visible from s relative to R² minus C.
A parenthesis asserts mathring C is nonempty because Gamma intersect mathring T nonempty implies card(Gamma intersect ]s',s''[) is at least two.

An edge alpha containing y is chosen. Lemma V is invoked for visibility of all its points. A triangle with vertices z,z',z'' is used in an attempted endpoint argument, ending with visibility of z' and c.q-f.d.
The written conditional uses z',z'' in the base interval although alpha was [z,z']; the conclusion visibly uses S'(Gamma). Both are retained as written.

The corollary asserts the existence of a pair of distinct polygon vertices, one visible from the other relative to R² minus Gamma, with their open joining segment contained in the boundary of the convex hull.
Pencil interventions object to the claimed convex object and propose selecting a vertex at maximal distance from the line through s',s''; uncertainty in the marginal connecting signs is retained.
